newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA BIOCHIMBANK HIKES CAPITAL TO 16.8 BLN LVS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA BIOCHIMBANK HIKES CAPITAL TO 16.8 BLN LVS.

text.p: Bulgaria's Biochim bank raised its capital to 16.76 billion levs from 1.89 billion levs through a new share issue, a bank official said.

"Biochim share capital was increased to 16.76 billion levs through a payment made by the Bank Consolidation Company in dollar-denominated domestic bad loan bonds," Biochim executive director Vladimir Georgiev told shareholders.

The Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) made the payment through the bonds worth $82 million, allocated to Biochim under a government decision to improve capital to risk assets ratio of seven state-owned banks in June.

The capital rise through the bonds and retrieved credits of 14.5 billion levs allowed the bank to increase its capital to risk assets ratio to a positive 2.51 percent by October 31 from minus 1.6 percent at the end of 1995, Georgiev said.
After the capital rise the BCC, which manages state equity in local commercial banks, holds more than 99 percent of Biochim bank.
Biochim bank's assets now amount to 126.8 billion levs. It was set up through a merger of Biohim bank, Sofia bank and Serdika bank in August last year.

The bank continued sufferring lack of provisions. It set aside at least 16 billion levs in provisions against non-performing loans of around 29 billion levs as required under central bank regulations.

The shareholders' meeting of Biochim bank accepted the resignation of Vladimir Zheglov, the economic adviser of Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, as a member of the bank's supervisory board, Georgiev said.
The shareholders decided not to free from responsibility Milka Stefanova and Nikolai Pavunchev for last year's annual report due to violations of banking regulations.
Stefanova and Pavunchev were executive directors of Serdika bank, which merged into Biochim.

The sharehodlers delayed freeing from responsibility Biohim bank executive directors Anna Sabeva, Angel Stankov and Rositza Tosheva until a bank's internal audit was completed. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
